sources: dossier=net position 'Messages ARE nodes at runtime' (2026-06-19+2026-06-22, transcript): 'populate its bag from the body verbatim, let the scheduler settle it via the pure-cascade path, firing standard terminal/success cascade' — body population is a pre-settle step, not carried in the terminal/success payload; doc=message.md:30 claimed terminal/success payload carries the body as attributes_delta; code=lib/runtime/pure_cascade_settle.go:31 sets attributes_delta to an empty map; lib/runtime/message_delivery.go:172-178 populates the bag via NodeAttributes().Upsert + SetDispatchInputBag before the pure_cascade settle runs
note: Directly verified in code: pure_cascade_settle.go builds an empty attributes_delta; the body reaches the attribute bag earlier, via the delivery-time upsert. The dossier's own description of the mechanism (bag populated 'verbatim' at delivery, cascade merely 'firing standard terminal/success') matches code and contradicts the doc's stale claim. Rewrote message.md:30 to state the correct mechanism.

sources: dossier=intentional absences: 'Dead-lettering of unmatched messages ... superseded by the typed registry's loud 400 refusal of undeclared types' establishes receipt-time rejection is the only sanctioned dead-letter-adjacent behavior; delivery-time missing-receiver handling is a separate, undocumented-in-dossier defensive path; doc=message.md:23 Owns clause described dead-letter as firing on 'no subscribers' with dispatch still occurring and a standard audit-event row written; code=lib/runtime/message_delivery.go:148-159 deliverNamedMessageInTx: dead-letter fires when findMessageReceiverNode returns nil (missing receiver node), logs a Warn, and returns nil with no run created, no dispatch, no ledger row
note: Verified directly in code: the only 'dead letter' code path triggers on a missing message-receiver-node row, not an absence of subscribers, and it short-circuits before any run or event row is created. The doc's description of both the trigger condition and the consequence was wrong. Rewrote the Owns clause in message.md:23 to match observed code behavior; this doesn't touch the dossier's intentional-absence ruling on receipt-time dead-lettering, which is a different (retired) mechanism.

sources: dossier=required behaviors, publisher capability check (2026-05-17+2026-06-02, artifact) says 'resolve publisher_subscription_id against an active row'; design-corpus=concepts/publisher-subscription.md:36 (the owning concept for this exact check) is explicit: 'accepting active and mounting rows (a fast publisher can send its first message before the reconciler records the flip to active; rejecting it would drop a legitimate observation)'; doc=message.md:32 said 'live, active binding'; code=lib/control/controlapi/messages.go:189-190 accepts State==Active OR State==Mounting, sentinel text 'not live (active or mounting)'
note: publisher-subscription.md is the concept that owns this invariant and explicitly documents Mounting acceptance with rationale (avoid dropping a fast publisher's first message); code matches that design corpus exactly. The dossier's shorthand 'active row' is not in conflict — it predates the more precise sibling-concept articulation and isn't exhaustive language ruling Mounting out. message.md's 'live, active' phrasing was the stale/incomplete one. Fixed message.md:32 to state active-or-mounting, aligned with publisher-subscription.md's phrasing.
